name: Compact Desk with Drawer
pitch: A real desk cut to your room: panel legs with robot-vac clearance, a rear stretcher, hidden-joint drawer, monitor shelf and a cable slot.

stages.title: Cut the sheets
stages.detail: Fit-test coupon first (slot = tab + 0.1 mm), then cut 1 sheet(s): 39 m of cut path. The 1200 x 600 TOP is the biggest part; keep it flat on the honeycomb and cut inside-out.

stages.title: Remove char and sand
stages.detail: Brush char off every edge, 120 then 180 grit; round the desktop edge by hand (about 3 mm). Sand the side-panel windows.

stages.title: Dry fit the frame
stages.detail: Stand SIDE-L and SIDE-R, slide the BACK-STRETCHER into both, add the DRAWER-DIVIDER and FRONT-APRON, then drop the TOP over all the tabs. Check the tab ends are flush with the desktop and the legs stand square.

stages.title: Dry fit drawer
stages.detail: Assemble the drawer (finger corners, bottom with 4 tabs, face) and slide it on the two LEDGERs; it should run freely with 1.5 mm side play. Sand the finger pull slots.

stages.title: Pre-finish
stages.detail: Oil or poly the desktop top, the drawer, and the inside faces now; mask the tabs and slots so the glue bonds.

stages.title: Glue-up frame (Titebond III)
stages.detail: Glue the stretcher, apron, divider and ledgers into SIDE-L/R and the divider, then fit the TOP onto the tabs and clamp across the width. Wipe squeeze-out; 30 min clamp, 24 h before heavy use.

stages.title: Screws as clamps
stages.detail: 10 #8 x 1-1/2 in and 2 #8 x 1-1/4 in screws (3.0 mm pilots pre-cut): through each side face into the back stretcher edge; the drawer corners, bottom and face as the nightstand drawer.

stages.title: Monitor shelf and cable slot
stages.detail: Glue MON-UP-L/R into their top slots (they stand on the desktop and their tabs come through underneath), then the MON-SHELF onto their upper tabs. Edge-band or sand the cable slot.

stages.title: Wall stabilizer / cleat (optional)
stages.detail: Screw a Z-bar half to the rear face of the BACK-STRETCHER and the other half into studs to stop the desk creeping or wobbling. It is a stabilizer, not a floating-desk mount.

stages.title: Finish and pack
stages.detail: Last coat, 24 h cure, felt pads under the 4 feet, load-test 60 kg on the desktop centre, flat-pack with corner guards (parts up to 1.2 m).

materials.sheet: 18 mm (3/4 in) birch or Baltic-birch plywood, 4 x 8 ft x 1 (hardwood-ply top is a CNC upgrade)
materials.finish: hardwax oil or water-based poly, 3 coats on the top (about $15)

safety: Rated target 60 kg distributed on the desktop - UNVERIFIED; sag-test a 1200 mm top with 20 kg at the centre.
Top is held only by through-tabs and glue: let the glue cure 24 h before loading.
Stand-height (1000 mm) builds are less stable: fit the wall stabilizer and widen the stance (depth >= 650).

profit.labels: ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ONLY - not quotes, not guaranteed
profit.assumptions: All dollar figures are planning ESTIMATES / ASSUMPTIONS, not quotes, not guaranteed. Sheet prices: 4x8 ft 18 mm birch plywood $70-110, basic plywood $55-75 (assumption). Machine feed 100-200 mm/min is an UNVERIFIED estimate (ACMER publishes no 18 mm ply feed rate). Machine wear/electricity $1.70 per machine-hour (assumption). Labor valued at $25/h for the "after labor" line only. Marketplace fees 10% (assumption, e.g. Etsy-style).
profit.price_band_source: SHORTLIST.md: custom target $250-$600 (estimate); small computer desks widely sold ~$100-$400 [third-party estimates]
profit.note_machine_time: At 100-200 mm/min the laser path alone is 3.3-6.5 machine hours per unit; machine time, not material, is the bottleneck. Verify the real feed on scrap before quoting.

unverified: Desktop deflection with 18 mm ply over 1200 mm not tested; rear stretcher and divider are the only stiffeners.
Laser feed 100-200 mm/min on 18 mm ply is an estimate.
Visible tab ends on the desktop surface (sand flush / cover with a desk mat or veneer).
Drawer slides on plywood ledgers (no hardware slides).
Price band is an estimate from SHORTLIST.md.
